content:
Hi! I'm interested in formalizing basic random walk theory in Mathlib. I wanted to check what exists and get feedback on the approach before starting.

What I've found so far:

  • Mathlib has iIndepFun, IdentDistrib, martingale theory, Borel-Cantelli, CLT, and strong law — so the building blocks are there.
  • There is no RandomWalk definition or partial sum process in Mathlib.
  • Rémy Degenne's brownian-motion project has stochastic process infrastructure but no discrete random walks.

Proposed approach:

  • Start by defining the partial sum process $S_n = \sum_{i < n} X_i$ as a general construction.
  • Initial plan: definition, martingale property, gambler's ruin, recurrence of $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}^2$, transience of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d \geq 3$.

Question:
Would you suggest that I start with the simplest setup in which X_i's are i.i.d. \pm 1, or would you suggest I immediately start with the most general possible situation.

Thanks in advance for any suggestions!

Hi! I don't know what is your lean background, but if you are a beginner I would suggest that you focus on formalizing a result you want without worrying at all about contributing to Mathlib.

Regarding what we would want into Mathlib, I'd say we want a definition of discrete time random walks, I am wondering whether we can unify random walks on groups and on graphs in a nice way to avoid duplication.
